thesis.problem: Millions of employees in Germany, Italy and Spain are owed a tax refund and never claim it, because the return assumes vocabulary and paperwork most people do not have. The alternatives are a tax adviser whose fee can exceed the refund, or desktop software that still expects the user to know which boxes apply to them.
thesis.solution: Taxfix replaces the form with a guided set of plain-language questions, selecting only the ones that fit the answers already given, and files the return for a flat fee once the refund is shown. The company is deliberately aimed at simple tax situations — salaried people with a payslip — rather than at the complex cases advisers are built for.

sources.title: Taxfix, the Berlin-based mobile tax filing app, raises $220M at a $1B+ valuation
sources.quote: It has closed a Series D of $220 million at a valuation of over $1 billion, money that the startup will be using both to build in more products to extend its touch points with customers beyond annual use around tax time; and to expand to new markets beyond its current footprint of Germany, Spain and Italy.

sources.title: Berlin's Taxfix lands $65 million Series C led by Index Ventures to grow automated tax return app
sources.quote: Taxfix, a Berlin-based automated tax software, has raised a $65 million Series C led by Index Ventures, with support from existing investors Valar Ventures, Creandum and Redalpine.
